notes.claim: Turning the rotor makes a rotating magnetic field, which induces a three-phase voltage in the stator winding.
A three-phase alternator has three single-phase windings spaced so that the voltage in each phase is displaced by 120° from the other two.
The rotor speed fixes the frequency: a two-pole machine must turn at 3600 rpm to make 60 Hz.

sources.title: Lecture 6: Synchronous machines — egr.unlv.edu
sources.quote: The rotor is then turned by external means producing a rotating magnetic field, which induces a 3-phase voltage within the stator winding.

sources.title: Chapter 2 ABFC Power Plant Operations and Procedures — media.defense.gov
sources.quote: The three-phase alternator, as the name implies, has three single-phase windings spaced such that the voltage induced in any one phase is displaced by 120° from the other two.

sources.title: Lecture 4 — aast.edu
sources.quote: to generate 60-Hz power in a two-pole machine, the rotor _must_ turn at 3600 rpm.
